title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 1-3 of this chapter): there is a set \(\mathfrak{M}\) of 'multiplicités' (manifold-like pieces or strata), ordered by incidence \(\le\) (Y ≤ X: Y is a sub-multiplicity of X, a stratum incident to X). There is also a set \(\mathfrak{F}\) of 'figures', into which \(\mathfrak{M}\) embeds (1.2). Formula (1.3) gave two maps:
(a) \(F \mapsto \tilde F = \{X \in \mathfrak{M} \mid X \le F\}\), from \(\mathfrak{F}\) to \(\mathfrak{P}(\mathfrak{M})\), which is injective.
(b) A map from \(\mathfrak{F}\) to 'figures ensemblistes' \(\mathrm{Fig}(M)\).
Restricted to \(\mathfrak{M}\), (a) is \(X \mapsto \tilde X = \{Y \mid Y \le X\}\) (1.5), so a multiplicity corresponds to its closed down-set, not to \(\{X\}\).

This page adds a second, finer relation \(\ll\) on \(\mathfrak{F}\), read X ≪ F: 'X is truly (vraiment) in F', presumably 'genuinely' or 'generically' contained rather than merely incident or boundary-contained. It gives two new maps (1.6):
(a) The shadow \(\mathrm{Omb}_{\mathfrak{M}}(F) = \{X \in \mathfrak{M} \mid X \ll F\} \subset \mathfrak{M}\), called the ombre or grande ombre of F.
(b) The multi-shadow \(\mathrm{Multomb}_{\mathfrak{M}}(F) \in \mathrm{Fig}(\mathfrak{M}) \subset \mathfrak{P}\mathfrak{P}(\mathfrak{M})\). By (1.7), read correctly, this is \(\mathrm{Multomb}(F) = \{\mathrm{Omb}(X) \mid X \in \tilde F\}\): the family of shadows of all multiplicities incident to F. Here, by (1.8), \(\mathrm{Omb}(X) = \{Y \in \mathfrak{M} \mid Y \ll X\}\), the analogue of (1.5) with \(\ll\) in place of \(\le\).

Claims:
- (a) need not be injective; a figure is not determined by the multiplicities truly inside it, since lower-dimensional or boundary parts may be invisible to the shadow.
- (b) is injective. Proof sketch: if \(\ll\) is an order (in particular reflexive) on \(\mathfrak{M}\), then X is the largest element of Omb(X) for \(\ll\). So Omb is injective on \(\mathfrak{M}\), and Multomb(F) recovers \(\tilde F\), which recovers F by injectivity of (1.3a).

The next page pulls these back along \(L \hookrightarrow M\) to get the 'small' shadow and multi-shadow (1.9).

Purpose: to set up ways of coding figures by subsets and families of subsets of the set of multiplicities. This serves the 1986 'Analysis situs' project of a combinatorial or tame foundation for stratified geometric figures.
errors: The written form of (1.7), '{X ∈ F̃ | Omb X}', is not a well-formed set-builder. It must mean {Omb(X) | X ∈ F̃}; otherwise Multomb(F) would not lie in PP(M) as (1.6 b) requires.
Label mismatch: (1.8) is introduced as the explicit form of Omb(X), but its left-hand side is written Mult(·)omb(X) with a correction. The intended left side is Omb(X).

Injectivity of (1.6 b) silently requires that \(\ll\) be reflexive (or at least that X be recoverable from {Y | Y ≪ X}) on multiplicities. It also uses injectivity of F ↦ F̃. Neither is stated on this page, though 'relation d'ordre' suggests reflexivity.

ideas.what: Shadow of a figure: the set of multiplicities 'truly contained' in F for a second order relation \(\ll\), distinct from the incidence order \(\le\).
ideas.modern_name: Down-set (order ideal) for a strict or interior-type containment relation; comparable to 'way-below' sets ↡x in domain theory, or open-star/interior conditions in stratified spaces.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Order-theoretic down-sets are folklore; way-below is due to Scott and the continuous-lattice school (c. 1972-80).

ideas.what: Encoding a figure injectively by the family of shadows of its incident multiplicities (multi-shadow), as an element of PP(M).
ideas.modern_name: Injective coding of a stratified set by a family of down-sets (a set-system representation).

ideas.what: Distinction between large shadow (on M) and small shadow (pulled back to L ⊂ M), the latter tending to be injective in the multi version.
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of incidence data to a subposet (e.g., to a generating class of strata).
ideas.where_published: Related themes (tame topology, stratified structures) appear in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6, but not this formalism.

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open whether the shadow map F ↦ Omb(F) is injective. He proposes the multi-shadow as an injective replacement but does not characterise the image of Fig(M), nor when small shadows suffice. This is a minor foundational thread of his 1986 tame-geometry (Analysis situs) project, which was never developed publicly.
missed.quote: Il n'est pas clair que cette application F → P(M) soit injective
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest. It documents a combinatorial, poset-theoretic approach to stratified 'figures' that is close in spirit to later work on o-minimal stratifications and to combinatorial models of stratified spaces (exit-path posets), but it adds no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: This page sets up elementary definitions: shadows as down-sets for a second order relation, and an injective multi-shadow coding. It is a nice glimpse of the vocabulary of the unpublished 1986 Analysis situs project ('ombre', 'multiombre', 'vraiment dans'), but the mathematics is routine order theory with no substantive result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'il y a deux autres applications'; 'autres' is inserted above the line.
(1.6 b) reads roughly 'F ↪ PP(M) et = F → Fig(M) ⊂ PP(M)'. The crossed-out word before Multomb_M(F) is a false start, 'Mult'.

Read 'ou la grande ombre de F', and 'Une multiplicité X qui est dans la grande ombre d'une figure F est dite "vraiment dans" la figure F'. 'L'ombre multistrate' and 'vraiment la figure' are misreadings.
Read 'qui se déduit de a) via la formation de F̃'.
(1.7) has a crossed-out old label '(1.5)'. The content should read Multomb(F) = {Omb X | X ∈ F̃}.
Read 'utiliser la relation d'ordre ≪ au lieu de ≤', followed by a struck-out fragment.
